## Metabolomics data cleaning and preparation workflow

### Goal:

To prepare and quality check raw metabolomic data prior to downstream metabolomics analyses (e.g. WGCNA, differential abundance analysis, etc...)

### About:

This workflow uses the "MetCleaning" R package to clean up and prepare MS peak spectra data prior to statistical analysis. Please refer to the [manual](https://github.com/MetabLAB/MetCleaning/blob/master/vignettes/MetCleaning.pdf) for further information. This workflow assumes that you are starting with a table of unannotated compounds and their MS peak intensities. Based off of the TidyMass tutorial [(here)](https://www.tidymass.org/docs/chapter2/1-create_mass_dataset/).

### **This workflow:**

1.  [Workspace Preparation]
2.  [Data reading and preparation]
3.  [Explore dataset]
4.  [Data cleaning]
5.  [Technical variable correction]
6.  [Save the cleaned data]

![](https://media.springernature.com/full/springer-static/image/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41467-022-32155-w/MediaObjects/41467_2022_32155_Fig3_HTML.png?as=webp)

[Note: An important decision point in this script, is whether to keep or remove outliers (4. Data cleaning: Identify and remove outliers). Be sure to check results before moving to the next step.]{underline}

### Input Files Preparation
For more information, see "Chapter 2 massDataset package" from the Tidymass online tutorial.

## Data reading and preparation

### Prepare the CSV files

This workflow requires [three files for each ionization mode]{.underline}: 
(1) sample_info: a LCMS run metadata table 
(2) variable_info: a sample metadata table to be extracted from expression_data, and 
(3) expression_data: an ionization peaks table. We are also including (4) sample_groups for additional analysis including all metadata. Parameters for each file type are detailed below.

Note that your [sample IDs must match exactly across all files]{.underline} and [sample_info must match the compound ID in the associated expression data table]{.underline}.

**sample_info:** The columns `sample_id` (sample ID), `injection.order` (injection order of samples), `class` (Blank, QC, Subject, etc), and `batch` (batch number) are required.

**variable_info:** The columns `variable_id` (variable ID), `mz` (mass to charge ratio), `rt` (retention time, units are in seconds) are required.

**expression_data:** The columns `variable_id` (compound ID), `mz` (mass to charge ratio), `rt` (retention time, units are in seconds), and your expression data (where column names are your sample IDs) are required. Other compound information (e.g. isotope distribution) may also be included, but is not required.

**sample_groups:** The columns `sample_id` (sample ID) and `group` (control, treatment1, treatment2, etc) are required.


### Load Prepared CSV Files & Extract Datasets

Path to input files
```{r}
in_path <- "3-Metabolomic_workflow/1-Montipora/1-Input"
```

```{r}
peak_table_pos = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "1-Positive_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_pos_expression_data.csv"))
peak_table_neg = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "2-Negative_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_neg_expression_data.csv"))

sample_info_pos = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "1-Positive_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_pos_sample_info.csv"))
sample_info_neg = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "2-Negative_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_neg_sample_info.csv"))

sample_groups_pos = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "1-Positive_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_pos_sample_groups.csv"))
sample_groups_neg = read_csv(file.path(in_path, "2-Negative_ionization/U23_tidymass_mont_neg_sample_groups.csv"))

#Add sample group information to sample info
sample_info_pos <- left_join(sample_info_pos, sample_groups_pos, by="sample_id")
sample_info_neg <- left_join(sample_info_neg, sample_groups_neg, by="sample_id")
```


Variable (metabolite) information (e.g. mass-to-charge ration ("mz"), retention time ("rt), isotope distribution ("isotope.dist")) and expression data are in the peak tables, so we have to separate them

[Positive]{.underline}
```{r}
expression_data_pos  <-  
  peak_table_pos %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(variable_id:isotope.dist)) %>% #minus bc want all other cols 
  as.data.frame() ; head(expression_data_pos)

variable_info_pos = 
  peak_table_pos %>% 
  dplyr::select(variable_id:isotope.dist) %>% 
  as.data.frame(); head(variable_info_pos)

rownames(expression_data_pos) <-  variable_info_pos$variable_id; head(expression_data_pos) 

expression_data_pos[expression_data_pos == 0] <- NA #NA is missing data
#rows are metabolite names, columns are sample name
```

[Negative]{.underline}
```{r}
expression_data_neg  <-  
  peak_table_neg %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(variable_id:isotope.dist)) %>% 
  as.data.frame() ; head(expression_data_neg)

variable_info_neg = 
  peak_table_neg %>% 
  dplyr::select(variable_id:isotope.dist) %>% 
  as.data.frame(); head(variable_info_neg)

rownames(expression_data_neg) <-  variable_info_neg$variable_id; head(expression_data_neg) 

expression_data_neg[expression_data_neg == 0] <- NA
```

Make sure that rowname and colname orders match up. 
If output is false, then cols dont match row names (could be extra col, etc). Check where and remove from the CSV files

```{r}
expression_data_pos = 
  expression_data_pos[,sample_info_pos$sample_id]
all(diff(match(colnames(expression_data_pos),sample_info_pos$sample_id)) > 0)

expression_data_neg = 
  expression_data_neg[,sample_info_neg$sample_id]
all(diff(match(colnames(expression_data_neg),sample_info_neg$sample_id)) > 0)
```

Verify the dataset qualities
```{r}
ncol(expression_data_pos)
length(sample_groups_pos$sample_id)
setdiff(colnames(expression_data_pos), sample_groups_pos$sample_id)

ncol(expression_data_neg)
length(sample_groups_neg$sample_id)
setdiff(colnames(expression_data_neg), sample_groups_neg$sample_id)
```

### Create mass_data class object for each ionization mode

```{r}
object_pos <-
  create_mass_dataset(
    expression_data = expression_data_pos,
    sample_info = sample_info_pos,
    variable_info = variable_info_pos
  )
object_pos
```


```{r}
object_neg <-
  create_mass_dataset(
    expression_data = expression_data_neg,
    sample_info = sample_info_neg,
    variable_info = variable_info_neg
  )
object_neg
```

## Data cleaning
For more information, see "Chapter 6 Data cleaning" from the Tidymass online tutorial.

Change batch to character.

```{r}
object_pos <- 
  object_pos %>% 
  activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(batch = as.character(batch))

object_neg <- 
  object_neg %>% 
  activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(batch = as.character(batch))

```

### Pre-cleaning report

Create a report of raw data quality. Save as HTML. It is recommended to review the HTML report for the pre-cleaned dataset before moving forward.

```{r}
object_pos@sample_info$class <- gsub("Sample", "Subject", object_pos@sample_info$class)
massqc::massqc_report(object = object_pos,
                      path = "3-Metabolomic_workflow/1-Montipora/3-Output/Pos_data_quality_pre_cleanup")
object_neg@sample_info$class <- gsub("Sample", "Subject", object_neg@sample_info$class)
massqc::massqc_report(object = object_neg,
                      path = "3-Metabolomic_workflow/1-Montipora/3-Output/Neg_data_quality_pre_cleanup")
```

### Filter out noisy metabolites

#### Positive

Check MVpercentage before noisy feature removal
```{r}
show_variable_missing_values(object = object_pos %>% 
                               activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info"), 
                             percentage = TRUE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.01, 2))
```

Filter such that metabolites with a missingness frequency of 40% or higher across all samples are removed
```{r}
MV.lim = 0.4 #standard missing value threshold for Montipora

nfeatures_before <- nrow(extract_variable_info(object_pos))

object_pos =
  object_pos %>%
  mutate_variable_na_freq()

object_pos <-
  object_pos %>%
  activate_mass_dataset(what = "variable_info") %>%
  filter(na_freq < MV.lim)

nfeatures_after <- nrow(extract_variable_info(object_pos))
```

Check the before and after to verify and quantify MVs removed
```{r}
#Check before and after
nfeatures_before
nfeatures_after
nfeatures_before - nfeatures_after #total MVs removed
```

Check MVpercentage after noisy feature removal
```{r}
show_variable_missing_values(object = object_pos %>% 
                               activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info"), 
                             percentage = TRUE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.01, 2))
```

#### Negative

Check MVpercentage before noisy feature removal
```{r}
show_variable_missing_values(object = object_neg %>% 
                               activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info"), 
                             percentage = TRUE) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.01, 2))
```

Filter such that metabolites with a missingness frequency of 40% or higher across all samples are removed 
```{r}
MV.lim = 0.4 #standard missing value threshold for Montipora

nfeatures_before <- nrow(extract_variable_info(object_neg))

object_neg =
  object_neg %>%
  mutate_variable_na_freq()

object_neg <-
  object_neg %>%

  filter(na_freq < MV.lim)

nfeatures_after <- nrow(extract_variable_info(object_neg))
```

### Identify and remove outlier samples

[Outlier detection]{.underline}

Visualize the samples

Positive
```{r}
massdataset::show_sample_missing_values(object = object_pos,
                                        color_by = "group",
                                        order_by = "injection.order",
                                        percentage = TRUE) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 2)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 2)) +
  ggsci::scale_color_aaas()

```
Negative
```{r}
massdataset::show_sample_missing_values(object = object_neg,
                                        color_by = "group",
                                        order_by = "injection.order",
                                        percentage = TRUE) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 2)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 2)) +
  ggsci::scale_color_aaas()

```


Detect outliers in samples

Positive
```{r}
outlier_samples_pos =
  object_pos %>%
  `+`(1) %>% 
  log(2) %>%
  scale() %>%
  detect_outlier(); outlier_samples_pos
```

```{r}
outlier_table_pos <- extract_outlier_table(outlier_samples_pos) %>%
  apply(1, function(x){
    sum(x)
  }) %>%
  `>`(1) %>%
  which()
outlier_table_pos
```

12 positive outliers detected. (need to be identified in 2/4 of the tidymass tests)

Negative
```{r}
outlier_samples_neg =
  object_neg %>%
  `+`(1) %>% 
  log(2) %>%
  scale() %>%
  detect_outlier(); outlier_samples_neg
```

```{r}
outlier_table_neg <- extract_outlier_table(outlier_samples_neg) %>%
  apply(1, function(x){
    sum(x)
  }) %>%
  `>`(1) %>%
  which()
outlier_table_neg
```
15 negative outliers detected. (need to be identified in 2/4 of the tidymass tests)

[Outlier removal]{.underline}

If outliers were detected in *either* ionization mode, they should be removed from *both* so as not to skew the results. 

Outliers are removed if they meet the requirements of 2/4 of the masscleaner tests (according_to_na, according_to_pc_sd, according_to_pc_mad, accordint_to_distance)

Positive:
We detected 12 samples as outliers in the positive ionization, so we will remove them from both datasets.

Negative:
We detected 15 samples as outliers in the negative ionization, so we will remove them from both datasets.

Combine all outliers into one list.
```{r}
outlier_table_all <- c(outlier_table_pos, outlier_table_neg)
```

[Remove from Positive Dataset]{.underline}

```{r}
nrow(extract_sample_info(object_pos)) #number of samples before

object_pos <- object_pos %>%
  activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info") %>%
  filter(!sample_id%in%names(outlier_table_all))

nrow(extract_sample_info(object_pos)) #number of samples after
```

Check the results of removing outliers
```{r}
pos_exp_mat <- extract_expression_data(object_pos)
pos_exp_mat[is.na(pos_exp_mat)] <- 0
pca <- prcomp(t(pos_exp_mat), scale. = F)

percentVar <- pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2) #save % variation by PC1 and PC2

pos_pca <- data.frame(extract_sample_info(object_pos), pca$x) #make a dataframe containing all plotting info
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = pos_pca, aes_string(x = "PC1", y = "PC2")) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(shape=group, colour=group)) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", round(percentVar[1] * 100), "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", round(percentVar[2] * 100), "% variance")) +
  coord_fixed() 
```

[Remove from Negative Dataset]{.underline}
```{r}
nrow(extract_sample_info(object_neg)) #number of samples before

object_neg <- object_neg %>%
  activate_mass_dataset(what = "sample_info") %>%
  filter(!sample_id%in%names(outlier_table_all))

nrow(extract_sample_info(object_neg)) #number of samples after
```
Check the results of removing outliers
```{r}
neg_exp_mat <- extract_expression_data(object_neg)
neg_exp_mat[is.na(neg_exp_mat)] <- 0
pca <- prcomp(t(neg_exp_mat), scale. = F)

percentVar <- pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2) #save % variation by PC1 and PC2

neg_pca <- data.frame(extract_sample_info(object_neg), pca$x) #make a dataframe containing all plotting info
```


```{r}
ggplot(data = neg_pca, aes_string(x = "PC1", y = "PC2")) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(shape=group, colour=group)) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", round(percentVar[1] * 100), "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", round(percentVar[2] * 100), "% variance")) +
  coord_fixed() 
```

### Missing value imputation

Here, we use the random forest method to impute missing values for our two datasets. Sampling methods, such as random forest, have been shown to be the most robust method for imputing missing values in datasets with low structure and with outliers [](https://bmcbioinformatics.biomedcentral.com/articles/10.1186/s12859-019-3110-0). Knn is a good backup option when you have high structure and low computational power.

#### [Positive]{.underline}
```{r}
get_mv_number(object_pos)

object_pos <- impute_mv(object = object_pos, method = "rf")

get_mv_number(object_pos)
```

Check data variation
```{r}
pos_exp_mat <- extract_expression_data(object_pos)
pos_exp_mat[is.na(pos_exp_mat)] <- 0
pca <- prcomp(t(pos_exp_mat), scale. = F)

percentVar <- pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2) #save % variation by PC1 and PC2

pos_pca <- data.frame(extract_sample_info(object_pos), pca$x) #make a dataframe containing all plotting info
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = pos_pca, aes_string(x = "PC1", y = "PC2")) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(shape=group, colour=group)) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", round(percentVar[1] * 100), "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", round(percentVar[2] * 100), "% variance")) +
  coord_fixed() 
```

#### [Negative]{.underline}

### Data normalization and integration

Data normalization and integration by the median method. Cannot use QC-based methods like SVR or Loess because we don’t have any QC samples. Play around with the median and mean options and see what works best for your data.

#### Positive

```{r}
object_pos <- 
  normalize_data(object_pos, method = "median")

object_pos2 <- 
  integrate_data(object_pos, method = "subject_median")
```

Visualize the normalization method. May have to go back to the last step and try a different method to compare.

```{r}
object_pos2 %>% 
  `+`(1) %>% 
  log(2) %>% 
  massqc::massqc_pca(color_by = "batch", line = FALSE)
```

```{r}
pos_exp_mat <- extract_expression_data(object_pos2)
pos_exp_mat[is.na(pos_exp_mat)] <- 0
pca <- prcomp(t(pos_exp_mat), scale. = F)

percentVar <- pca$sdev^2/sum(pca$sdev^2) #save % variation by PC1 and PC2

pos_pca <- data.frame(extract_sample_info(object_pos2), pca$x) #make a dataframe containing all plotting info
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = pos_pca, aes_string(x = "PC1", y = "PC2")) + 
  geom_point(size = 3, aes(shape=group, colour=group)) +
  xlab(paste0("PC1: ", round(percentVar[1] * 100), "% variance")) +
  ylab(paste0("PC2: ", round(percentVar[2] * 100), "% variance")) +
  coord_fixed() 
```

Plot compound mass-to-charge ratio against retention time
```{r}

  log(10) %>%
  show_mz_rt_plot() +

```

```{r}
  `+`(1) %>%
```

```{r}
  show_mz_rt_plot() +
  ggtitle("Negative ionization mode") +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.01, 2)); neg_plot
```

Create a report of raw data quality. Save as HTML.

```{r, echo=F}
massqc::massqc_report(object = object_neg2, path = "3-Metabolomic_workflow/1-Montipora/3-Output/Neg_data_quality_post_cleanup")
```

## Technical variable correction

### Re-load the data
```{r}
#positive
EDPC <- object_pos2@expression_data
    EDPC <- log(EDPC) %>% t()
MPC <- object_pos2@sample_info
    MPC <- MPC %>% mutate(Ion_mode = "Positive Ionization") %>% mutate(Data_type = "Cleaned Data")
#negative
EDNC <- object_neg2@expression_data
    EDNC <- log(EDNC) %>% t()
MNC <- object_neg2@sample_info
    MNC <- MNC %>% mutate(Ion_mode = "Negative Ionization") %>% mutate(Data_type = "Cleaned Data")
```

### PCA before correction

PCA Function
```{r}
PCA_loc_ggplot <- function(PC_plot, var_plot, title) {
    ggplot(PC_plot, 
    aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = injection.order)) +
    geom_point() +
    ggtitle(paste("PCA: ", title, PC_plot$group,"-",  PC_plot$Ion_mode)) +
    xlab(paste0("PC1: ", var_plot$PC1, "% variance")) +
    ylab(paste0("PC2: ", var_plot$PC2, "% variance")) +
    xlim(-120, 120) +
    ylim(-120, 120) +
    theme_bw() + #Set background color
    theme(panel.border = element_blank(), # Set border
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", size = 0.6), #Set axes color
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = 10, face = "bold"), #Axis title size
        plot.background=element_blank(), #Set the plot background
        plot.title = element_text(color="black", size=14, face="bold")
)
}
```

Positive
```{r}
results.EDPC <- prcomp(EDPC, scale = TRUE) #calculate principal components
results.EDPC$rotation <- -1*results.EDPC$rotation #reverse the signs
results.EDPC$x <- -1*results.EDPC$x #reverse the signs of the scores
PC.EDPC <- as.data.frame(results.EDPC$x) #store in a data frame
PC.EDPC.summary <- summary(results.EDPC) #check the proportion of variance
variance.EDPC = (results.EDPC$sdev^2 / sum(results.EDPC$sdev^2))*100 #pull out total variance explained by each principal component
variance.EDPC <- as.data.frame(variance.EDPC) #store variance in a dataframe
variance.EDPC$PCs <- colnames(PC.EDPC)

#reorient and store for ggplots
var_plot.EDPC <- variance.EDPC
var_plot.EDPC$variance.EDPC <- round(var_plot.EDPC$variance.EDPC, digits = 0)
var_plot.EDPC <- as.data.frame(t(var_plot.EDPC))
colnames(var_plot.EDPC) <- var_plot.EDPC[2,]
PC_plot.EDPC <- PC.EDPC
PC_plot.EDPC$sample_id <- rownames(PC_plot.EDPC)

#add qualities to metadata to make easier to plot
PC_plot.EDPC <- full_join(PC_plot.EDPC, MPC, by = "sample_id")

#plot
PCA_plot.EDPC <- PCA_loc_ggplot(PC_plot = PC_plot.EDPC, var_plot = var_plot.EDPC, title = "injection.order bias present - Montipora - Positive"); PCA_plot.EDPC
```

### Get rid of technical bias

Positive
```{r}
library(limma)
MPC_corr <- MPC %>% dplyr::select(injection.order, sample_id)
row.names(MPC_corr) <- MPC$sample_id

MPC_corr <- MPC_corr[row.names(EDPC),]
MPC_corr <- as.data.frame(lapply(MPC_corr, factor))
MPC_corr <- as.data.frame(lapply(MPC_corr, as.numeric))

design <- model.matrix(~sample_id + injection.order, data = MPC_corr)
sample_id.design <- design[, 1:2]
batch.design <- design[, -(1:2)]
corr.data.pos <- removeBatchEffect(t(EDPC), design = sample_id.design, covariates = batch.design)

EDPC.cln      <- corr.data.pos
EDPC.cln.save <- corr.data.pos
```

Negative
```{r}
MNC_corr <- MNC %>% dplyr::select(injection.order, sample_id)
row.names(MNC_corr) <- MNC$sample_id

MNC_corr <- MNC_corr[row.names(EDNC),]
MNC_corr <- as.data.frame(lapply(MNC_corr, factor))
MNC_corr <- as.data.frame(lapply(MNC_corr, as.numeric))

design <- model.matrix(~sample_id + injection.order, data = MNC_corr)
sample_id.design <- design[, 1:2]
batch.design <- design[, -(1:2)]
corr.data.neg <- removeBatchEffect(t(EDNC), design = sample_id.design, covariates = batch.design)

EDNC.cln      <- corr.data.neg
EDNC.cln.save <- corr.data.neg
```

### PCA after correction

## Positive

Re-orient data for PCA
```{r}
EDPC.cln[EDPC.cln < 0] <- 1
EDPC.cln <- log(EDPC.cln) %>% t()
#remove metabolites w/o variance
sds <- apply(EDPC.cln, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) # Check for variance using std deviation
names(sds)[sds == 0] # Print columns that have a standard deviation of 0
EDPC.cln <- EDPC.cln[, apply(EDPC.cln, 2, sd, na.rm = TRUE) > 0] # Keep only columns w/ variance
```

```{r}
results.EDPC.cln <- prcomp(EDPC.cln, scale = TRUE) #calculate principal components
```


# 4. Make the final tidymass object

Positive tidymass object
```{r}
EDPC.cln.save <- as.data.frame(EDPC.cln.save)
sample_info_pos <- object_pos2@sample_info
variable_info_pos <- object_pos2@variable_info

object_pos3 =
    create_mass_dataset(
        expression_data = EDPC.cln.save,
        sample_info = sample_info_pos,
        variable_info = variable_info_pos
    )
```

Negative tidymass object
```{r}
EDNC.cln.save <- as.data.frame(EDNC.cln.save)
sample_info_neg <- object_neg2@sample_info
variable_info_neg <- object_neg2@variable_info

object_neg3 =
    create_mass_dataset(
        expression_data = EDNC.cln.save,
        sample_info = sample_info_neg,
        variable_info = variable_info_neg
    )
```
